original_text:
–Domain Bacteria–are the most diverse and widespread prokaryotes.–Prokaryotes are organisms lacking membrane bound nucleus
–Domain Archaea–are prokaryotes that often live in Earth’s extreme environments.–Deep sea vents, volcanic chambers, etc
–Domain Eukarya–All organisms are eukaryotes, or contain a membrane bound nucleus–Range from single-celled protists to multicellular organisms
explanation: This slide compares the three domains of life. Domain Bacteria contains the most diverse and widespread prokaryotes. Prokaryotes are defined as organisms that lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Domain Archaea contains prokaryotes that frequently live in Earth's extreme environments, such as deep-sea vents and volcanic chambers. Domain Eukarya consists of eukaryotes, meaning all its organisms possess a membrane-bound nucleus; this domain ranges from single-celled protists to multicellular organisms.

questions.q: What is the defining difference between prokaryotes and eukaryotes as described on this slide?
opts: Prokaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotes lack one.
Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotes contain a membrane-bound nucleus.
Prokaryotes are always multicellular, while eukaryotes are single-celled.
Prokaryotes live in extreme environments, while eukaryotes do not.
questions.exp: The slide defines prokaryotes as 'organisms lacking membrane bound nucleus' and eukaryotes as organisms that 'contain a membrane bound nucleus'.

questions.q: Which domain contains organisms that often live in extreme environments like deep-sea vents and volcanic chambers?
questions.exp: The slide states: 'Domain Archaea – are prokaryotes that often live in Earth’s extreme environments. – Deep sea vents, volcanic chambers, etc'.
